solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Athenian character's black mark for wasting time

definitions.note: read as 'Athenian character is', a letter of the Greek alphabet

indicators.note: wasting here means losing or using up, so the time abbreviation is dropped from the mark

parts.note: a stigma is a mark of disgrace

explanation.surface: An ancient Greek is rebuked for idling away the hours.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', linking definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Sigma is the eighteenth letter of the Greek alphabet, used in Athens as elsewhere in Greece.

clue.text: One who is out and about

definitions.text: One who is out and about

parts.words: One who is out and about
parts.note: out means asleep and about means walking around: a person wandering while unconscious

explanation.surface: A description of someone sociable and on the move.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out and about' suggests a busy socialite, but 'out' here means fast asleep.
explanation.definitionFit: A sleepwalker walks about while out cold, asleep in bed in all but body.

clue.text: Soldier's second mechanical device?

parts.note: a GI is an American soldier, with the possessive S
a mo is a moment, a second

explanation.surface: A soldier's gadget is described as belonging to the second in command.
explanation.definitionFit: A gismo, or gizmo, is slang for any gadget or contraption whose name one forgets.

clue.text: Female set of books a young lout's written all over?

parts.note: Ann is a woman's name
OT is the Old Testament, a set of books of the Bible
a Ted, or Teddy boy, was a 1950s British youth gang member

explanation.surface: A woman's books have been scribbled on by a delinquent youth.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'has'. A Teddy boy was a 1950s British youth in Edwardian-style dress, often seen as a hooligan.
explanation.definitionFit: A text that is annotated has notes written over it, the question mark flagging the playful reading.

clue.text: Large pad of hair behind back-to-front cap

indicators.note: placing the hair word behind puts it after the cap
worn back to front, the word for the cap is written in reverse

parts.note: a tam is a Scottish woollen cap, a tam-o'-shanter
a tress is a lock of hair

explanation.surface: A hairpiece sits under a cap worn the wrong way round.
explanation.definitionFit: A mattress is a large cushioned pad to sleep on.

clue.text: Poor performer upset and no longer fired up — one dealing with jumbo?

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset turns the word upside down, so it is read from the bottom up

parts.note: a ham is an overacting, poor actor
a fire that is no longer lit is out

explanation.surface: A bad actor loses enthusiasm, and the clue wonders if he handles a jumbo jet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jumbo' suggests a jet, but here it is an elephant.
explanation.definitionFit: A mahout is an elephant keeper and driver in South Asia.

clue.text: Wilder man of the stage? Yesteryear's character leading fashion

indicators.note: the old letter comes first, leading the fashion word

parts.note: thorn is an Old English letter, a character from long ago
ton means fashion or style

explanation.surface: An unruly actor, with an old-fashioned figure setting trends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wilder' looks like a comparative of wild but is a surname.
explanation.definitionFit: Thornton Wilder was an American playwright, author of Our Town.

clue.text: Rodent, one being caught on a food dish

indicators.note: the numeral is caught inside the rodent word

parts.note: a rat is a rodent
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A rat is caught on a plate of food.
explanation.definitionFit: Raita is an Indian side dish of yoghurt with cucumber or herbs.

clue.text: More dependable VIP protecting a French revolutionary

indicators.note: the celebrity word surrounds the rest, as a bodyguard protects

parts.note: a star is a very important person
un is French for a
Che Guevara, the Argentine revolutionary

explanation.surface: A celebrity guards a French rebel and seems more reliable.
explanation.definitionFit: Staunch means loyal and dependable, so staunchER is the comparative.

clue.text: Top criminal has turned cynical towards other people

indicators.note: turned means twisted round, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A leading crook has become disillusioned with humanity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Criminal' looks like the anagram signal but is part of the fodder; 'turned' is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A misanthrope distrusts or dislikes humankind in general.

clue.text: Time to start doing without has dawned, yes, sadly

indicators.note: sadly suggests things have gone wrong, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone glumly notes the morning they begin a fast has arrived.
explanation.definitionFit: Ash Wednesday begins Lent, a season of giving things up.

clue.text: Change of opinion regarding performance

parts.note: about means concerning, regarding
a turn is an act or performance on stage

explanation.surface: A shift in view about how an act went.
explanation.definitionFit: A complete reversal of position, from the military drill command to face the other way.

clue.text: Woman needing a good comfy home for the most part

indicators.note: only most of the word is used, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: a nest is a snug home

explanation.surface: A woman wants a pleasant, cosy place to live, mostly.
explanation.definitionFit: Agnes is a female given name.

clue.text: Cries from characters in trouble at school

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the run of words, as characters within them

explanation.surface: Wailing pupils who have been told off at school.
explanation.definitionFit: Bleats are the plaintive cries of sheep or goats, or feeble complaints.

clue.text: Report of the decline of first female spy

indicators.note: a report is something heard, so the words are spoken

parts.note: Eve was the first woman, and a drop is a decline: Eve's drop

explanation.surface: A news item about the downfall of the original woman spy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spy' is a verb here, and 'Report' signals sound.
explanation.definitionFit: To eavesdrop is to listen secretly to a private conversation.

clue.text: Give convincing evidence of travel to exhibition

parts.note: to go is to travel
a show is an exhibition

explanation.surface: Proof of a journey to a display.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something goes to show a point means it demonstrates it.

clue.text: Public individuals offering added nuances

parts.note: overt means open, done in public
ones are single units, individuals

explanation.surface: Figures in public life provide subtler shades of meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: Overtones are subtle implications beyond the literal meaning.

clue.text: Cricket side embarrassed about fellow awaiting trial

parts.note: the on side, or leg side, is half of a cricket field

indicators.note: the colour word goes about, around, the man

parts.note: red-faced, as one blushes
a man is a fellow

explanation.surface: A cricket team blushes about a man.
explanation.definitionFit: A prisoner held on remand is in custody until trial.

clue.text: Sweetheart getting nothing achieved

parts.note: love is zero in tennis scoring
done means accomplished

explanation.surface: A darling who accomplishes nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A loved one is a person one cherishes, a partner or family member.

clue.text: Was in awe of agent holding attention

indicators.note: the agent word holds the other inside it

parts.note: a fed is a US federal agent
to have someone's ear is to have their attention

explanation.surface: An admiring secret agent who keeps people listening.
explanation.definitionFit: To fear something can mean to hold it in reverent awe.

clue.text: One duck and another escaping from open vehicle

indicators.note: one letter escapes, leaving the vehicle word without it

parts.note: a scooter is a small open motor vehicle
another duck, a cricket score of nought, is O

explanation.surface: Two ducks, one fleeing a convertible car.
explanation.walkthrough: A duck in cricket is a score of zero, so 'another' duck is the letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: The scoter is a dark sea duck.

clue.text: A girl suffering setback needs the ultimate in moral fibre

indicators.note: a setback sends the words backwards

parts.note: sis is short for sister

indicators.note: ultimate means last, so only the final letter is used

explanation.surface: A girl's troubles need the final degree of moral strength.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moral fibre' reads as a phrase, but 'fibre' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Sisal is a plant fibre used for rope and matting.

clue.text: Money the attraction that traps Conservative

indicators.note: the attraction word encloses the letter as a trap holds its prey

parts.note: a lure is an attraction

explanation.surface: Cash is the bait that catches a Tory.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucre is money, especially gained dishonourably, as in filthy lucre.

clue.text: Hot-headed and no longer worth quoting

parts.note: ex means former, no longer
citable means fit to be cited, quoted

explanation.surface: A firebrand whose words are no longer quotable.
explanation.definitionFit: Excitable means easily roused to anger or passion.

clue.text: Location of Jacob's ladder? Not hard to see plant

indicators.note: not here means without, so the letter is left out

parts.note: in Genesis, Jacob dreamt of the ladder at Bethel
H is the abbreviation for hard, as in pencils

explanation.surface: A biblical place, made easy to spot a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Betel is an Asian climbing plant whose leaves are chewed with areca nut.

clue.text: Put off road trip, ascent being hazardous

indicators.note: a hazardous course is chaotic, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A drive was postponed because the uphill climb was dangerous.
explanation.definitionFit: To procrastinate is to delay or postpone action.

clue.text: Second page reached by customer of paper that covers a wide area

definitions.note: read as 'thing that covers a wide area', a noun

parts.note: a newspaper's customer is its reader

explanation.surface: A newspaper's second page is seen by a buyer of a paper with broad coverage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reached by' just links the pieces in order.
explanation.definitionFit: A spreader is a device that scatters material, such as fertiliser, across a broad field.

clue.text: Charge for trip

definitions.meaning: a sudden rush forward, a sortie by troops

explanation.definitionFit: A sally is both a military charge out from a besieged place and a jaunt or excursion.
